2_Introduction: The devices exhibited an increased PCE from 18.4601% to 18.4601%, with a VOC of 1.1251 V, FF of 73.7463%, and JSC of 22.248 mA/cm². A 1.5 mol/L Cs0.1FA0.9PbI2.8Br0.2 precursor solution was similarly prepared using a mixture of DMF and DMSO. The perovskite solutions were spin-coated at 1200 rpm for 10 s and 5000 rpm for 30 s, respectively. During the second step, 200 µL of chlorobenzene was dropped on the spinning substrate 8 s before the end of the process. The film was subsequently annealed at 110 °C for 30 min.
3_Result_Discussion: The perovskite layer, formulated as Cs₀.₁FA₀.₉PbI₂.₈Br₀.₂, adopts a mixed-cation, mixed-halide ABX₃ structure where the partial Cs⁺ substitution at the A-site enhances phase stability and suppresses halide segregation by tightening the Goldschmidt tolerance factor (≈0.92), while the Br⁻ incorporation at the X-site widens the bandgap slightly and mitigates I⁻ vacancy formation and ion migration under operational bias; crystallization is critically governed by the dual-spin protocol—initial low-speed (1200 rpm) deposition enabling uniform precursor wetting and nucleation onset, followed by high-speed (5000 rpm) shear-driven solvent expulsion that, when coupled with precisely timed antisolvent quenching (200 µL chlorobenzene at 8 s pre-end), triggers instantaneous supersaturation and arrests Ostwald ripening, thereby yielding compact, pinhole-free films with enlarged grains and reduced grain boundary density; however, the absence of any molecular additive, surface-anchoring self-assembled monolayer (SAM), or defect passivator in the described process means no targeted suppression of undercoordinated Pb²⁺ at grain boundaries, no energetic alignment tuning at the charge transport interface, no dipole-induced band-bending to facilitate hole extraction or electron blocking, and no chemical passivation of halide vacancies or interstitial iodides—consequently, non-radiative recombination remains unmitigated at both bulk and interfacial sites, carrier lifetimes are intrinsically limited by trap-assisted Shockley–Read–Hall pathways, and interfacial energy level misalignment persists, all of which collectively constrain open-circuit voltage and fill factor despite nominally favorable morphology implied by the standard annealing (110 °C, 30 min) that fully volatilizes DMSO and consolidates the α-phase without residual PbI₂ (as would be evident from absent ~12.6° XRD peaks) or δ-phase signatures; critically, the reported PCE remains unchanged at 18.4601%, with VOC = 1.1251 V, FF = 73.7463%, and JSC = 22.248 mA/cm², confirming that the baseline processing—though reproducible—lacks any functional molecular intervention to modulate nucleation thermodynamics, passivate electronic traps, or engineer interfacial dipoles, thus leaving performance pinned at the intrinsic limit imposed by unpassivated ionic defects and unoptimized energy-level cascades.
